name: Guinea

findings.local_actor: SOGEB (Société de Gestion et d'Exploitation du Backbone National)
findings.builder: Huawei Technologies (with Tactis, France, on design)
findings.summary: Huawei built Guinea's national fibre backbone (about 4,000–4,500 km, with data and monitoring centres) under a China Eximbank loan covering 90% of a US$238m cost; state operator SOGEB launched commercial service in September 2020.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole prc: Huawei is the equipment vendor and designer. Still current: Ecofin (May 2026) reports SOGEB raising backbone capacity to 400 Gb/s with Huawei technical support, target 600 Gb/s by end-2026. Length figures vary across sources (3,987 / 4,352 / 4,500 km). US$238m is total project cost per AidData and Financial Afrik.

findings.controller: Government of Guinea (SOGEB backbone data centres)
findings.summary: AidData records that the Huawei-built national backbone project included data centres and network monitoring centres, completed around April 2020.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded facilities as the buildings are owned by the state SPV SOGEB (pole domestic); Huawei is builder. IT equipment inside is presumably Huawei (prc) but not stated. Single opened source; number, size and current use of these data centres unknown.

findings.summary: A US$50m China Eximbank loan, on-lent to state operator SOTELGUI, financed a Huawei-implemented modernisation and 2G-to-4G fibre upgrade; AidData lists it as completed by December 2020 but notes operational status is unclear.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 3, not 5: AidData itself doubts the 4G upgrade became operational (no 4G network in early 2019). Pre-2020 commitment; still_current not established and SOTELGUI's present operating status was not checked in this run. Single opened source.

findings.local_actor: Government of Guinea (Ministries of Plan, Security and Civil Protection)
findings.financier: Export-Import Bank of China (385.3m yuan concessional loan, 2%, 20 years)
findings.summary: Guinea signed a China-financed agreement for a 'Guinea Safe City' video-surveillance network covering Conakry's 13 communes and other cities: 324 camera sites, eight command centres and a dedicated LTE network; the transitional parliament approved the loan in March 2026.
findings.analyst_inference: Huawei is named as vendor only by AllAfrica; WeAreTech (Apr 2024) shows Guinea asked Huawei to implement the Guinea Safe City programme. Ecofin and Guinéenews do not name a vendor, so the pole rests on that attribution. Value: AllAfrica/Guinéenews give EUR 50m; Ecofin gives 385.3m yuan, about US$56m (Ecofin's conversion). Tier 3 (signed, ratified financing agreement); no construction start confirmed. Guinéenews (May 2025) said deployment was under way, unverified.

findings.summary: The same Safe City financing includes six LTE base stations for a dedicated security-forces wireless network, plus 900 portable and 100 vehicle terminals.
findings.analyst_inference: Vendor inferred from the Safe City bundle (Huawei per AllAfrica); Ecofin names no vendor. Single opened source for the LTE component.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy, Guinea
findings.summary: Guinea's digital minister signed an MOU with Huawei in Beijing covering high-speed and rural fibre networks, e-government, data centres, cybersecurity and ICT training; a July 2026 ministerial meeting discussed a future state cloud, with no instrument signed.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 1 non-binding MOU spanning several layers; coded networks as its most concrete strand. CapMad (July 2026) says formal agreements and financing remain undefined. Corroboration not met: CapMad covers a later meeting, not the 2024 MOU.

findings.controller: Government of Guinea (Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy)
findings.summary: Guinea inaugurated its first national data centre, a 600 m² facility with Uptime Institute Tier III design certification, alongside relaunch of the .gn domain, in Conakry in September 2025.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole domestic assumed: government-inaugurated, but neither source names owner-operator, builder, financier or IT-equipment vendor. A COREX executive spoke at the launch; COREX's role unknown. Small facility; tier 5 means inaugurated and in service, not large-scale.
